newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr chased lower by stop-loss hunters.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr chased lower by stop-loss hunters.

text.p: The Australian dollar had its nosed pressed to support at the midsession after coming under pressure from speculators hungry to trigger stop loss sales.
Traders said a failed rally to US$0.7420 overnight had left some players a little long and they were squeezed out of those positions this morning.

Talk further stop loss orders were crowded beneath US$0.7360 tempted banks into going short in the hope of triggering a sizeable selloff, but so far bids had proved solid there. A breach would target key support at US$0.7330/40 and put the 18-month trough of US$0.7310 at risk.
By 12.15 pm (0215 GMT) it had been hounded to US$0.7365/70 from an early US$0.7373/78 and US$0.7392/97 late here Tuesday.

The sellers were encouraged by a bearish technical outlook following the failure to sustain a short covering rally past 75 cents last week. To many, the pullback confirmed the currency's four month old downtrend from 80 cents had further to run and couyld yet reach the chart target of US$0.7250, if not the 1995 trough of US$0.7070.
A rally back above US$0.7440 was counter the immediate pressure and it would take a break of both US$0.7505 and US$0.7550 resistance to reverse the trend.
The currency was also burdened by uncertainty over monetary policy which had not been entirely settled by last week's long expected rate cut.

Most analysts thought this probably was the last in the cycle, but few were willing to rule out yet another given signs of economic activity were mixed at best and the only certain bet was that underlying inflation would stay near record lows for a few quarters yet.
The lacklustre nature of the leconomy was illustrated by the NAB July business survey which found conditions deteriorated in July, so losing all the modest improvement made in June.

The survey found some small improvements in business conditions for retailing, wholesaling, construction and transport. But these were more than offset by a deterioration in services and manufacturing.
Labour shedding also increased, with the employment index down at negative five from negative one in June.

This was alarming for dollar bulls since official labour data for July are due Thursday and any weakness was certain to kindle talk of another easing. Analysts expect jobs growth to pick up to around 25,000 in July from a modest 11,900 in June, but even then it would not compensate for May's 40,300 fall.

Anything less than a 20,000 increase in employment would be considered soft and a fall -- which no analyst was looking for but none would rule out given the volatility of this series -- would see the money market begin to price in another rate cut.

Elsewhere, the local dollar held firm on the mark at 1.3854/70 from 1.3808/21 after hitting a six year high atop 1.3900 overnight after the Bundesbank passed up a chance to fire a policy warning shot about the mark's weakness.
It was also up at 87.99/09 yen from 87.62/72 but eased to 58.0 in trade weighted terms from 58.1.
